The orchard that grows forty kinds of pear

On a slope above the river there is an orchard where every tree is a different variety of pear, planted by a retired engineer who wanted to know which ones would still fruit after a cold spring.

Twelve years later he has an answer of sorts. About a third of the trees fruit reliably, a third sulk, and the rest produce in alternate years, apparently at random.

Members of the local fruit group now visit every autumn to taste them.
